mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return tends to be positive due to reduced policy tightening expectations and increased risk appetite.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the same period (t-test p > 0.05) during qualifying months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) predicts a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as labor market strength supports corporate earnings optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly above the 95th percentile of prior tightening cycles (quantile regression).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 3% for three consecutive months is associated with a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals expanding economic activity and demand for equity risk assets.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO increases by ≥3% each month for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During qualifying INDPRO expansion, 20-day forward returns are not higher than the 10th percentile of all prior similar expansion windows (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in a given month, the S&P 500 5-day forward return tends to be negative as investors anticipate future rate hikes and demand for safe assets rises.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3.0 in a given month (unexpected vs prior month)
failure_condition: Over 20 such inflation spikes, the average 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than the mean of all other inflation surprise periods (two-sample t-test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the monthly ratio of residential housing starts (HOUST) by at least 10% compared to the prior month predicts a negative S&P 500 20-day forward return as it signals cooling construction activity and reduced economic momentum.
failure_condition: During housing contraction months, 20-day forward returns are not more negative than the 5th percentile of all contraction months (quantile analysis).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in both unemployment (UNRATE) and underemployment (PAYEMS) by at least 0.2 percentage points and 5,000 jobs, respectively, over two months, create a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as it signals a more resilient labor market.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by ≥0.2pp and PAYEMS decreases by ≥5,000 over two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns during such labor resilience episodes are not statistically higher than during baseline periods (bootstrapped p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; therefore, this sketch is omitted to comply with the proxy constraint). Instead, a proxy-based alternative: When monthly industrial production (INDPRO) falls by more than 4% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is likely negative due to demand softening and risk aversion.
Note: This sketch is included for completeness but uses only available proxies. In practice, only demand proxies present in the catalog should be used.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥4% each month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such INDPRO declines, 20-day forward returns are not more negative than the 10th percentile of prior demand-softening episodes (rolling quantile).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly change in the monetary base growth rate (implied via FEDFUNDS dynamics) turns positive for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return tends to be positive as it reflects expectations of future liquidity easing and reduced policy tightening pressure.
candidate_trigger: First difference of FEDFUNDS turns positive for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 such transitions, the average 60-day forward return is not higher than the 50th percentile of all prior transitions (bootstrapped percentile).
